sampling_model.design: Four independent destructive population snapshots at times \(0,h,2h,3h\).
sampling_model.units: At time \(kh\), \(n_k\) independent units are sampled from the marginal law of \(Y_k\); no unit is followed across time.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is present; the structural target is the continuous-time interaction generator \(G\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Sample means and covariances form \(\widehat z\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\). On a regular noncyclic finite branch, the local residual projection gives \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\); globally certified initialization and labeling remain the explicit open question.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.1 characterizes and generically selects a transition from two covariance congruences and mean equations when the propagated noise covariance is known.
Corollary 2.1 states that three time points identify the transition and constant load under its known-noise conditions.
Theorems 6 and 8 recover deterministic affine dynamics from two supplied covariance pairs and mean pairs under generic spectral and probe conditions.
Theorem 1 states that QWENDY returns the ground-truth linearized transition from four supplied covariance matrices under invertibility and simple-spectrum conditions.
Algorithms 1 and 2 alternate Schrödinger-bridge trajectory reconstruction with transition and process-noise updates for direct state snapshots.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify Newton convergence and equality or distinctness of supplied approximate roots of square polynomial systems.
The paper derives concentration and normal approximation for empirical spectral-projector error under Gaussian sampling.
Theorem 2.6 makes likelihood-ratio limits at semialgebraic boundaries and singularities depend on tangent cones.

body.tldr: Three independent Gaussian snapshots have an exact dimension-dependent identification frontier under one unknown common positive-definite measurement covariance.  When \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the raw \(O(1)\) torsor contains two opposite-determinant transitions, and the negative-determinant transition fails the principal-logarithm cut; model-compatible laws therefore identify the full explanation from three snapshots.  The exceptional \(d_0=0\) regime retains a continuous \(O(2)\) ambiguity.  For \(p\ge3\), three snapshots generically retain a continuous \(O(p-1)\) ambiguity, whereas a fourth snapshot generically identifies through the rational map \(K_1K_0^{-1}\).  In all dimensions, the four-snapshot block Gram certificate enumerates the raw stabilizer fiber, while stability, the logarithm cut, Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity determine structural compatibility.  Stabilizer dimension equals information nullity; on finite strata the exact attainable worst-case number of compatible explanations is \(2^{p-1}\).  The cyclic chart has explicit perturbation bounds and Gaussian moment inference, while globally implementable initialization and stable labeling on regular noncyclic finite strata remain open.  Supplying \(E\) yields this paper's stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves model, not equality with that model class.

project_justification.gap: Published snapshot-identification results either use supplied state covariances or work in broader known-noise transition models without classifying the fiber created by one unknown common additive covariance.  They do not expose the dimension-two elbow at which the two raw three-snapshot completions have opposite determinants and the principal-logarithm cut removes exactly one.  A supplied \(E\) places the present stable, embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise system inside the broader Aalto--Lamoline--Goncalves class, which also permits known process covariance, arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws; it does not make the two model classes equal.
project_justification.niche: Common measurement noise cancels from adjacent covariance differences but re-enters through level-covariance positivity.  With three snapshots this gives an exactly computable one-vector orthogonal matching problem: it generically collapses to one admissible explanation in dimension two through a determinant obstruction, leaves an \(O(2)\) continuum at zero displacement, and leaves positive-dimensional ambiguity generically in dimensions at least three.  The fourth snapshot adds a second congruence that generically collapses the higher-dimensional stabilizer through a rational Krylov identity.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the exact three-snapshot norm certificate and \(O(p-r)\) classification, including the sharp dimension-two determinant elbow; an if-and-only-if four-snapshot block Gram certificate; a bijective admissibility map; the complete exceptional-stratum classification; and the sharp attainable finite-fiber maximum \(2^{p-1}\), together with rational perturbation theory and branchwise inference.  It also identifies the precise supplied-noise subclass relation and retains certified global initialization and branch labeling as the remaining open construction problem.

body.related_work: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides the closest congruence architecture.  Its published class allows known process covariance \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time dynamics, and finite-second-moment non-Gaussian laws.  After a supplied measurement covariance \(E\) is subtracted, the model studied here is only its stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, \(Q=0\) subclass; the inherited consequence used here is the consecutive latent-covariance congruence, not equality of model classes or an exact reduction to every part of its theorem.  It does not provide the present unknown-common-noise norm certificate, the \(O(p-r)\) torsor, the dimension-two determinant selection, the two-probe residual-rank classification, or the sharp \(2^{p-1}\) admissible finite-fiber maximum.  WangEtAl2024 proves a three-time-point result for deterministic affine dynamics from supplied state moments and motivates the \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer, but supplied covariances remove the common-noise torsor and therefore do not reveal the \(p=2\) principal-logarithm elbow.  QWENDY2025 uses four supplied covariance matrices and simple spectra to resolve a homogeneous congruence problem, but it contains neither an unknown common additive covariance nor the exact three-snapshot classification proved here.  MorimotoKashima2025 and InoueEtAl2026 estimate stochastic linear dynamics from direct snapshot marginals by Schrodinger-bridge optimization without a global common-noise identification certificate.  Blevins2017 analyzes continuous-time aliases and motivates the principal-logarithm strip after the transition is recovered.  KoltchinskiiLounici2017 supplies spectral perturbation tools, while HauensteinSottile2012 supplies root certificates; neither solves basis-invariant finite-branch enumeration with matrix-inequality filters.  ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Drton2009 locate set inference and singular asymptotics around the regular-stratum results.  KongEtAl2023 studies process and measurement covariance identification from a paired stationary time series with known system matrices, a different information regime from destructive marginal snapshots.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact population conditions--spectral matching, block Gram equality, and the three-snapshot whitened norm equality--must not be imposed as empirical accept-or-reject equalities, because unconstrained noisy sample moments satisfy them with probability zero. On a finite population stratum, the block certificate yields \(2^q\) raw sign completions; when \(q\ge1\), the determinant test removes at least half before the principal-logarithm calculation, and the sharp worst-case number of admissible transition matrices is \(2^{p-1}\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is the off-model rational estimator used by the perturbation theorem. The radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) guarantees that its full plug-in reconstruction is defined, whereas the smaller radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) also preserves the stability, logarithm, Stein, and reconstructed-covariance positivity filters; neither radius forces noisy moments onto the exact population fiber. On a noncyclic finite stratum, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is a population-branch-centered residual estimator, not a globally implementable branch finder until certified initialization and labeling are solved. The two structural plug-ins are \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) and \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\), each with initial-mean coordinate \(\widehat m_0\).
body.honest_scope: The exact population three-snapshot norm certificate, its \(O(p-r)\) raw fibers, the dimension-two determinant elbow, the dimension-dependent three-versus-four frontier, stabilizer dimension, the sharp attainable finite-stratum maximum of \(2^{p-1}\) compatible explanations, the information-nullity identity, cyclic perturbation bounds, and the population-indexed local limit law under \(\gamma_W>0\) are theorem-level deliverables.  For model-compatible laws with \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), three snapshots identify the full explanation because only one of the two raw \(O(1)\) completions can pass the principal-logarithm cut; the condition \(d_0\ne0\) is generic in the mean parameter.  The \(d_0=0\) elbow retains continuous \(O(2)\) ambiguity in dimension two, and three snapshots retain continuous ambiguity generically for \(p\ge3\), where a fourth snapshot is generically necessary and is generically sufficient on the cyclic chart.  Any unknown-common-noise supermodel containing the deterministic Gaussian subclass inherits only these continuous nonidentification witnesses, not the dimension-two identified conclusion.  Supplying \(E\) gives only the stable, principal-log-embeddable, Gaussian, zero-process-noise subclass of AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022; the broader published class also permits known \(Q\), arbitrary invertible discrete-time transitions, and non-Gaussian finite-second-moment laws.  The global certified initializer, complete branch certificate, stable empirical labeling, and simultaneous coverage across all noncyclic finite branches remain open.  No uniform inference is claimed at branch collisions, positivity boundaries, logarithm cuts, or stabilizer-dimension jumps, and exact population equalities are not empirical testing rules.
